name: Tangier
hero_subtitle: Strait views, a layered medina and the meeting point of Atlantic and Mediterranean light.

info.vibe_val: Port city, strait winds and historic lanes
info.airport_val: TNG Ibn Battuta · Al Boraq to Rabat/Casa · Ferry from Spain

overview.title: Welcome to Tangier — gateway between Europe and Africa
overview.p1: Tangier sits where the Atlantic and the Mediterranean meet, with a medina that climbs toward the kasbah and a modern strip along the beach. It is a city of crossings — ferries from Spain, the Al Boraq train south, and day roads to Chefchaouen, Asilah and Tetouan.
overview.p2: Give yourself two or three days: medina and kasbah, Café Hafa on the cliffs, Cap Spartel and Hercules Caves to the west, and an easy seafront walk. Stay near the medina for atmosphere or on the corniche for beach access.

places.title: Must-visit places in Tangier
places.subtitle: Medina lanes, cliff cafés and Atlantic headlands.

medina.name: Tangier Medina
medina.desc: Whitewashed streets, Petit Socco and gates toward the kasbah.

kasbah.name: Kasbah Museum
kasbah.desc: Palace-museum on the hill with strait and roof views.

socco.name: Grand Socco
socco.desc: Main square between new town and medina gates.

hafa.name: Café Hafa
hafa.desc: Terraced mint-tea stop above the Strait of Gibraltar.

beach.name: Tangier Beach
beach.desc: Long urban corniche for walks and sea air.

spartel.name: Cap Spartel
spartel.desc: Lighthouse headland west of town, often with Hercules Caves.

caves.name: Hercules Caves
caves.desc: Coastal caves and the famous sea opening near Cap Spartel.

malabata.name: Cap Malabata
malabata.desc: Quieter headland looking back over Tangier bay.

legation.name: American Legation
legation.desc: Museum and courtyard inside the medina.

itinerary.title: 3 days in Tangier
itinerary.subtitle: A flexible outline — adjust for arrival time and day trips.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter from Grand Socco, wander the lanes and pause at Petit Socco for coffee.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Climb to the kasbah for the museum and terraces over the strait.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Mint tea on the cliff terraces as the light softens over the water.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Taxi west to the lighthouse headland where Atlantic horizons open.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Short stop at the sea caves and the famous opening toward the ocean.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Back in town for a medina restaurant or a quieter new-town option.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Tangier Beach or Cap Malabata
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Easy morning on the city beach / corniche, or east to Cap Malabata for open views.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — American Legation or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit the American Legation museum in the medina, or keep time for shopping and cafés.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Train or road links toward Rabat, Chefchaouen or the airport depending on your route.

stays.title: Where to stay in Tangier? Our favorites
stays.subtitle: Kasbah riads with strait views, a historic palace hotel, and a seafront resort on Malabata bay.

card1.name: La Tangerina
card1.desc: Iconic kasbah riad with terraces over the medina and the Strait of Gibraltar — a Tangier classic.

card2.name: Nord Pinus Tangier
card2.desc: Design hotel in the kasbah with bold interiors, pool and panoramic views toward Spain.

card3.name: Hotel El Minzah
card3.desc: Historic palace hotel near the Grand Socco — gardens, old-world charm and a central base for the medina.

card4.name: Mövenpick Hotel Malabata
card4.desc: Seafront resort on Malabata bay — pool, beach access and modern comfort outside the medina bustle.

booking_banner.title: Explore All Places to Stay in Tangier

eat.title: Where to eat in Tangier
eat.subtitle: Family tables, traditional tajines, port fish and mint tea — no bar scene.

nomad.title: Le Saveur de Poisson
nomad.desc: Famous no-menu seafood house — daily catch, shared tables and a pure Tangier classic for families.

jardin.title: Restaurant Hamadi
jardin.desc: Family-run traditional Moroccan tables in the medina — tajines, couscous and no bar scene.

fassia.title: Restaurant Al Andalous
fassia.desc: Simple family restaurant for couscous, grills and everyday Moroccan plates.

moha.title: Restaurant Assaada
moha.desc: Local grills and tajines near Petit Socco — casual, affordable and family-friendly.

bacha.title: Poissons du Port
bacha.desc: Fresh grilled fish by the fishing port — simple plates, families and local prices.

elfenn.title: Café Hafa
elfenn.desc: Cliff terraces for mint tea and sunset over the Strait — a family must, not a nightlife spot.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Petit taxis for short hops; agree meter or price. Walking works well in the medina and along the corniche.

bargain.title: Airport & train
bargain.desc: TNG Ibn Battuta airport serves the city. Al Boraq high-speed trains link Tangier with Rabat and Casablanca.

water.title: Day trips
water.desc: Chefchaouen, Asilah and Tetouan are the usual road outings; Cap Spartel is a half-day west of town.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Tangier
daytrips.subtitle: Blue medinas, Atlantic ramparts and Andalusian heritage within easy reach.

chefchaouen.name: Chefchaouen
chefchaouen.desc: Blue medina in the Rif — about 2–2.5 hours by road.

asilah.name: Asilah
asilah.desc: Atlantic medina and ramparts south of Tangier — about 1 hour.

tetouan.name: Tetouan
tetouan.desc: UNESCO medina and Andalusian heritage — about 1 hour east.

q1.question: How many days in Tangier?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the medina, kasbah, Café Hafa and Cap Spartel. A third day suits a beach morning or a trip to Asilah or Chefchaouen.

q2.question: Is Tangier only a transit city?
q2.answer: No — the medina, kasbah, Café Hafa and west-cape loop make it worth two or three nights on its own.

q3.question: How do I get to Tangier?
q3.answer: Tangier Ibn Battuta Airport (TNG), Al Boraq train from Rabat/Casablanca, and ferries from Spain.

q4.question: Best time to visit Tangier?
q4.answer: April–June and September–November for mild weather. Summer is warmer and busier; winter can be windy and wet.
